statement: O-1A classification requires extraordinary ability in science, education, business, or athletics, shown by sustained national or international acclaim and evidenced either by receipt of a major, internationally recognized award (such as the Nobel Prize) or by at least 3 of the 8 listed forms of documentation: nationally or internationally recognized prizes or awards for excellence; membership in associations requiring outstanding achievements as judged by recognized experts; published material about the person in professional or major trade publications or major media; judging the work of others in the field; original scientific, scholarly, or business-related contributions of major significance; authorship of scholarly articles; employment in a critical or essential capacity for organizations with a distinguished reputation; or a high salary or other remuneration, with comparable evidence allowed where these criteria do not readily apply to the occupation (8 CFR § 214.2(o)(3)(iii)).
caveat: Meeting 3 criteria is the evidentiary floor, not the outcome: USCIS weighs the totality of the record case-by-case and can find the sustained-acclaim standard unmet on qualifying paperwork, and the petition is filed by a US employer or agent, not the founder directly. This repo does not assess eligibility; immigration decisions need counsel.
